text: Choose the passive form of: The teacher praised the students.
options: The students were praised by the teacher.
The students are praised by the teacher.
The students was praised by the teacher.
The teacher was praised by the students.
explanation: The active verb is in the simple past, so the passive uses were plus the past participle, with the object as the new subject.

text: Choose the passive form of: She writes a letter.
options: A letter was written by her.
A letter is being written by her.
A letter is written by her.
A letter has been written by her.
explanation: The simple present active becomes is or are plus the past participle in the passive: is written.

text: Choose the active form of: The window was broken by the boy.
options: The boy breaks the window.
The boy had broken the window.
The boy broke the window.
The boy has broken the window.
explanation: The passive was broken is simple past, so the active verb is broke, with the boy as the subject.

text: Choose the passive form of: They are building a bridge.
options: A bridge was being built by them.
A bridge is built by them.
A bridge is being built by them.
A bridge has been built by them.
explanation: The present continuous active becomes is or are being plus the past participle: is being built.

text: Choose the passive form of the order: Open the door.
options: The door is opened.
The door was opened.
Let the door opened.
Let the door be opened.
explanation: An order in the active voice becomes Let ... be plus the past participle in the passive.

text: Choose the indirect form of: He said, "I am happy."
options: He said that he was happy.
He said that I was happy.
He said that he had been happy.
He said me that he was happy.
explanation: After a past reporting verb, the present am changes to was, and I changes to he.

text: Choose the indirect form of: She said to me, "Where do you live?"
options: She asked me where do I live.
She asked me where I lived.
She told me where I lived.
She asked me where I live did.
explanation: A question becomes asked, keeps normal word order with no do, and the tense moves back: where I lived.

text: Choose the indirect form of: The teacher said, "The earth moves around the sun."
options: The teacher said that the earth had moved around the sun.
The teacher said that the earth would move around the sun.
The teacher told that the earth moves around the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moves around the sun.
explanation: A universal truth keeps its present tense in indirect speech. The reporting verb said takes that, not told.

text: Choose the indirect form of: He said to her, "Please help me."
options: He requested her to help him.
He requested her to help me.
He ordered her to help him.
He asked her helping him.
explanation: A polite request uses requested, followed by to plus the verb, and me changes to him.

text: Arrange the parts into a meaningful sentence. P: The cat  Q: chased  R: the mouse  S: across the garden
options: PQRS
PRQS
QPRS
SPQR
explanation: The subject comes first, then the verb, then the object, then the place: The cat chased the mouse across the garden.

text: Arrange the parts into a meaningful sentence. P: has been  Q: for many years  R: Ravi  S: living in Delhi
options: RPSQ
PRSQ
RSPQ
QRPS
explanation: The sentence is: Ravi has been living in Delhi for many years. The subject comes first, then the verb group, then the place, then the time.

text: Arrange the sentences in the right order. P: Soon the whole village had gathered.  Q: A stranger set up a stall near the well one morning.  R: At first, nobody paid attention to him.  S: Then he began to play a flute.
options: QSRP
PQRS
RQSP
QRSP
explanation: The stranger arrives (Q), is ignored at first (R), then plays the flute (S), and soon a crowd gathers (P). The words At first, Then and Soon fix this order.

text: Arrange the sentences in the right order. P: As a result, the crops dried up.  Q: There was no rain for three months.  R: The farmers had to borrow money to buy seeds again.
options: PQR
QPR
RQP
QRP
explanation: The cause comes first (Q), then As a result gives the effect (P), and then the farmers' response (R).
